title: Given a new machine in BOOT, dispatch(ResetCompleted) moves it to INITIALIZING with behavior KeepInhibited (row D1)
preconditions: Freshly constructed machine; no guards wired
mocks: none
inputs: state = BOOT; event = ResetCompleted
steps: 1. Construct FlightStateMachine | 2. Call dispatch(ResetCompleted) | 3. Read the DispatchResult and state()
expected_result: outcome Accepted; from BOOT; to INITIALIZING; behavior KeepInhibited; row index is not -1; state() equals INITIALIZING
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on each DispatchResult field and on state()
notes: Parent ID for the permitted-row cases; rows D2 to D9 are separate NEW IDs because tc_id is unique. Expected values hand-written from SRS 10, not read from kTransitionTable. FR-061 tag is data only; output inhibit is enforced by SAF-01 (TC-BOOT-001).

evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on DispatchResult fields and state()

evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on DispatchResult fields and state(); fake call record
notes: SRS 10 row 4. Guard content is owned by STA-02 (TC-STATE-001). Only row that reaches ARMED (FR-067 context).

title: Given a newly constructed machine, state() is BOOT and an ArmRequest is rejected because no guard is wired
preconditions: Freshly constructed machine; no guards wired
mocks: none
inputs: no event before the first read; then event = ArmRequest
steps: 1. Construct FlightStateMachine | 2. Read state() | 3. Call dispatch(ArmRequest) | 4. Read the DispatchResult and state()
expected_result: state() equals BOOT after construction; dispatch(ArmRequest) returns RejectedNotPermitted; state() still equals BOOT
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on state() and outcome
notes: Hard rule: inhibited by default (FR-002, FR-061). No setter or constructor argument for the initial state, so this is verified by the public API only. Output inhibit itself is SAF-01 (TC-BOOT-001).

title: Given kTransitionTable, every key (from, event) is unique, every from and to is a valid enumerator, and exactly 9 rows exist
preconditions: Table is constexpr static data visible to the test
mocks: none
inputs: the full kTransitionTable
steps: 1. Iterate all rows and collect (from, event) keys | 2. Check each key is unique | 3. Check each from and to is one of the six FlightState enumerators and each event is one of the nine FlightEvent enumerators | 4. Count the rows
expected_result: no duplicate (from, event) key; all enumerators valid; row count equals 9
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on the row count and EXPECT_TRUE on uniqueness and enumerator checks
notes: Assumes the test can read kTransitionTable (design 4.1 lists it but does not state its visibility). The 9 and 6 and 9 counts come from design 4.1 and 4.2.

title: Given kTransitionTable, the only row whose to state is ARMED is D4 from DISARMED guarded by Arm
preconditions: Table is constexpr static data visible to the test
mocks: none
inputs: the full kTransitionTable
steps: 1. Iterate all rows | 2. Collect rows with to equal ARMED | 3. Inspect from, event, and guard of the collected rows
expected_result: exactly one row has to equal ARMED; its from is DISARMED, its event is ArmRequest, its guard is GuardId::Arm
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on the collected row count and fields
notes: Hard rule: no automatic re-arm (FR-067). Expected values written by hand, not derived from the table.

title: Given DISARMED and an Arm guard that denies, dispatch(ArmRequest) returns RejectedGuardDenied with the guard's reason and the state stays DISARMED (SRS 10 row 5)
preconditions: Machine in DISARMED reached via ResetCompleted and InitPassed; Arm guard wired with the denying fake
mocks: IStateGuard (fake): evaluate() returns allowed=false with a test-chosen opaque reason and records each (state, event) argument
inputs: state = DISARMED; event = ArmRequest; guard reason = test-chosen opaque value
steps: 1. Construct FlightStateMachine and wire the denying fake to GuardId::Arm | 2. Call dispatch(ResetCompleted) then dispatch(InitPassed) | 3. Call dispatch(ArmRequest) | 4. Read the DispatchResult and state()
expected_result: outcome RejectedGuardDenied; reason equals the fake's reason; state() equals DISARMED; fake recorded exactly one call with (DISARMED, ArmRequest)
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on outcome, reason, and state()
notes: Reason type is opaque uint16_t pending OQ-5 (STA-02, COR-03). Modeled as the guard-denied branch of D4 (OQ-6). Arm precondition content is STA-02 (TC-STATE-001).

title: Given a denying guard for each of D4, D8, and D9, dispatch returns RejectedGuardDenied and the state is unchanged
preconditions: Three machines, each forced to the from state of one guarded row; the matching guard wired with the denying fake
mocks: IStateGuard (fake): evaluate() returns allowed=false for every call and records each (state, event) argument
inputs: D4: DISARMED + ArmRequest; D8: FAILSAFE + RecoveryAccepted; D9: FAULT + ServiceReset
steps: 1. For each row force the machine to its from state through permitted events using an allowing guard for any earlier guarded step | 2. Wire the denying fake to the row's guard | 3. Call dispatch with the row's event | 4. Read the DispatchResult and state()
expected_result: for every row: outcome RejectedGuardDenied; state() equals the from state; fake recorded one call with (from state, event)
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on outcome and state() per row
notes: FR-067: a denied recovery guard cannot leave FAILSAFE or FAULT. Not asserting DispatchResult.row or to on a guard denial: the design does not define them (see open questions).

title: Given no guard wired for D4, D8, and D9, dispatch fails closed with RejectedGuardDenied and the state is unchanged
preconditions: Three machines, each forced to the from state of one guarded row; guard pointer for that row is null
mocks: none
inputs: D4: DISARMED + ArmRequest; D8: FAILSAFE + RecoveryAccepted; D9: FAULT + ServiceReset
steps: 1. For each row force the machine to its from state, wiring an allowing guard only to reach earlier states where needed | 2. Call setGuard(guard id, nullptr) for the row's guard | 3. Call dispatch with the row's event | 4. Read the DispatchResult and state()
expected_result: for every row: outcome RejectedGuardDenied; reason equals 0; state() equals the from state
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on outcome, reason, and state() per row
notes: Fail-closed default (design 4.3). Arm cannot succeed until STA-02 wires a real guard. Needs a way to reach ARMED and FAILSAFE and then clear the Arm guard: setGuard with null is assumed legal (design says null means unwired).

title: Given an event value outside the FlightEvent enumerators, dispatch returns RejectedInvalidInput, leaves the state unchanged, and calls no guard
preconditions: Machine in DISARMED; Arm guard wired with the allowing fake
mocks: IStateGuard (fake): evaluate() returns allowed=true for every call and records each (state, event) argument
inputs: event = static_cast<FlightEvent> of an integer beyond the last enumerator
steps: 1. Construct FlightStateMachine and wire the allowing Arm guard | 2. Reach DISARMED via dispatch(ResetCompleted), dispatch(InitPassed) | 3. Reset the fake's call record | 4. Call dispatch with the out-of-range event | 5. Read the DispatchResult, state(), and the fake's recorded calls
expected_result: outcome RejectedInvalidInput; state() equals DISARMED; fake recorded zero calls
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on outcome and state(); fake call count
notes: Hard rule: invalid input rejected with no change (FR-051, FR-054, NFR-016). The state machine never sees MAVLink bytes (design 4.3) and has no actuator interface, so no actuator mock applies. Exact out-of-range integer is a test choice, not a design value.

title: Given the last valid FlightEvent enumerator and the value one past it, dispatch classifies them as RejectedNotPermitted and RejectedInvalidInput respectively
preconditions: Machine in DISARMED; no guards wired
mocks: none
inputs: event = ServiceReset (last enumerator); event = static_cast<FlightEvent> of the integer one past ServiceReset
steps: 1. Construct FlightStateMachine and reach DISARMED | 2. Call dispatch(ServiceReset) and record the result | 3. Call dispatch with the value one past ServiceReset and record the result | 4. Read state() after each call
expected_result: first call: RejectedNotPermitted; second call: RejectedInvalidInput; state() equals DISARMED after both
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on outcome and state()
notes: Boundary of the enumerator range per design 4.2 step 1. Lower boundary (before the first enumerator) is not specified because the underlying type is not stated in the design.

title: Given each rejection cause, the three rejection outcomes are distinct enumerators and are not equal to Accepted
preconditions: Machine in DISARMED; Arm guard wired with the denying fake
mocks: IStateGuard (fake): evaluate() returns allowed=false for every call
inputs: not permitted: DisarmRequest in DISARMED; guard denied: ArmRequest in DISARMED; invalid input: out-of-range event
steps: 1. Construct FlightStateMachine and wire the denying fake to GuardId::Arm | 2. Reach DISARMED | 3. Call dispatch(DisarmRequest), dispatch(ArmRequest), and dispatch with an out-of-range event, recording each outcome | 4. Compare the three outcomes with each other and with Accepted
expected_result: outcomes are RejectedNotPermitted, RejectedGuardDenied, RejectedInvalidInput; all four values pairwise different; state() equals DISARMED after all calls
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ and EXPECT_NE on outcomes and state()
notes: Design test plan item: rejection outcomes are mutually distinguishable. DisarmRequest in DISARMED may be treated as a no-op by STA-03 (risk R-5); here it is RejectedNotPermitted.

title: Given BOOT or INITIALIZING and an allowing Arm guard, dispatch(ArmRequest) is rejected and the state is unchanged
preconditions: Two machines: one in BOOT, one in INITIALIZING; Arm guard wired with the allowing fake
mocks: IStateGuard (fake): evaluate() returns allowed=true for every call and records each (state, event) argument
inputs: state = BOOT then INITIALIZING; event = ArmRequest
steps: 1. Construct FlightStateMachine and wire the allowing fake to GuardId::Arm | 2. Call dispatch(ArmRequest) in BOOT and record the result | 3. Call dispatch(ResetCompleted) to reach INITIALIZING | 4. Call dispatch(ArmRequest) and record the result
expected_result: both calls: outcome RejectedNotPermitted; state() stays BOOT after the first and INITIALIZING after the second; fake recorded zero calls
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on outcome and state(); fake call count
notes: Hard rule: no path to ARMED before init completes (FR-002, FR-061). Output inhibit enforcement is SAF-01 (TC-BOOT-001).

title: Given each of the 45 non-permitted (state, event) pairs, dispatch returns RejectedNotPermitted, leaves state() unchanged, and calls no guard
preconditions: For each start state a fresh machine is forced there through permitted events; allowing fake wired to every GuardId
mocks: IStateGuard (fake): evaluate() returns allowed=true for every call and records each (state, event) argument
inputs: cross product of six states and nine events minus the nine permitted pairs
steps: 1. For each of the six start states construct a machine and wire the allowing fake to all GuardId values | 2. Force the start state with the permitted path through the public API | 3. Reset the fake's call record | 4. For each event not permitted in that state construct a fresh machine at the same start state and call dispatch(event) | 5. Read the DispatchResult, state(), and the fake's recorded calls
expected_result: for all 45 pairs: outcome RejectedNotPermitted; row index equals -1; state() equals the start state; fake recorded zero calls
evidence: gtest parameterized test with EXPECT_EQ on outcome, row, and state(); fake call count
notes: Parent ID for rejection cases; other rejection cases have their own NEW IDs. Pair list is hand-written from SRS 10, not read from the table. No state setter exists, so start states are forced through events.
